scenarios.hypothesis: A deterministic parser recovery transition resynchronizes after malformed synthetic metadata but leaves a partial semantic object trusted before required validation completes.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock read-only semantic consumer reports only synthetic object identity, incomplete flags, parser state generation, and validation status without external side effects.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic record with internally consistent metadata completes normal validation and produces a fully trusted read-only semantic object.
scenarios.negative_control: The same malformed synthetic record with recovery disabled is hard rejected before any semantic object reaches the downstream mock consumer.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if the fixture leaves the local owned parser harness, requires destructive payloads, or the consumer cannot remain read-only and synthetic.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After keeping incomplete state quarantined until validation finishes, the malformed recovery fixture is rejected while the valid positive control remains accepted.
scenarios.parser_input_phase_generation: Record input artifact identity, mutation generation, parser instance identity, parser configuration, recovery phase identity, and state generation for every transition.
scenarios.transition_invariant_trace: Capture the source state, recovery transition identity, expected invariant, observed incomplete invariant, target state, and first invalid trust-promotion transition.
scenarios.structural_metadata_semantic_object: Bind the inconsistent synthetic metadata fields to the exact partial semantic object identity and generation emitted after recovery resynchronization.
scenarios.recovery_deferred_validation_state: Record the recovery generation, incomplete flag, skipped or retained tokens, deferred-validation generation, and whether trust promotion occurs before validation.
scenarios.nested_cross_record_provenance: No nested parser is required; explicitly bind the single synthetic record and note that cross-record provenance is absent to isolate recovery behavior.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact mock read-only consumer that observes the partial semantic object and records whether it is treated as trusted or incomplete.
scenarios.effective_semantic_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to downstream read-only acceptance of one incomplete synthetic semantic object under the wrong trust state.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one structured in-memory receipt containing object identity, recovery generation, trust flag, and no external or persistent effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate input generation, parser instance, recovery transition, semantic object generation, downstream consumer, and read-only receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold input bytes, parser build, consumer, and metadata constant while changing only recovery enablement or validation-before-consumption ordering.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject harness failure, a different minimized phase path, instrumentation artifacts, intended permissive recovery, or safe later object reconstruction as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: PS3 because an inert downstream consumer accepts a synthetic semantic object produced under incomplete recovery state before required validation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PS3 maximum until a bounded semantic effect plus complete provenance, counterfactuals, receipts, and remediation replay support PS4 or PS5.

scenarios.hypothesis: Two valid synthetic duplicate records cause parser state to retain one selection policy while the downstream semantic resolver deterministically consumes the other record.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled read-only mock resolver returns only the selected synthetic record identity and semantic value, with no executable or external behavior.
scenarios.positive_control: A single-record synthetic fixture produces the same parser-state selection and downstream semantic selection with no duplicate ambiguity.
scenarios.negative_control: A duplicate fixture using the documented pinned selection policy converges on one record and yields matching parser and downstream identities.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort if duplicate semantics are not deterministic, the target contract explicitly permits both outcomes, or the fixture cannot remain synthetic and read-only.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After using one canonical duplicate-selection rule across parse and semantic phases, parser state and downstream resolver select the same synthetic record.
scenarios.parser_input_phase_generation: Record input artifact generation, parser instance, duplicate-processing phase, state generation, and the identity/generation of both duplicate records.
scenarios.transition_invariant_trace: Trace each duplicate-record transition, first/last-wins decision, expected selection invariant, and the first state where parser and semantic assumptions diverge.
scenarios.structural_metadata_semantic_object: Bind duplicate keys, ordering metadata, selected record identity, and resulting semantic object generation to the downstream selection result.
scenarios.recovery_deferred_validation_state: No recovery is required; record that validation completes normally so duplicate semantic selection is isolated from warning or recovery paths.
scenarios.nested_cross_record_provenance: Treat the duplicate records as cross-record candidates and record source ordering, duplicate policy, selection generation, and final linked semantic object.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the read-only semantic resolver that consumes the selected duplicate record and returns its synthetic identity as a structured result.
scenarios.effective_semantic_capability: The demonstrated capability is only a deterministic semantic-selection divergence for controlled synthetic records, not arbitrary execution or external access.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only synthetic semantic value identifying which duplicate record the final resolver consumed under the controlled fixture.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind record order, parser selection state, semantic resolver identity, selected record identity, and returned read-only value in one deterministic receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold both duplicate records constant and change only the documented first-wins versus last-wins selection rule, then compare parser and resolver convergence.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject nondeterministic container ordering, documented duplicate behavior, stale receipts, or a different parser instance as explanations for the selection divergence.
scenarios.evidence_level: PS4 because a bounded read-only semantic result is causally tied to the exact duplicate-order and parser-state selection tuple.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PS4 maximum until remediation replay plus complete parser, record, semantic-object, alternative-explanation, and receipt provenance satisfies PS5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A nested synthetic child structure remains parseable while parent and child length generations diverge across phases, producing an inconsistent child semantic view.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A synthetic in-memory parent and child parser with a read-only mock consumer reports only controlled region identity, lengths, and semantic-object generation.
scenarios.positive_control: Parent and child lengths that agree across all phase generations produce one consistent synthetic child semantic object and matching region identity.
scenarios.negative_control: A deliberately impossible child length is rejected at the framing boundary before nested semantic object construction or downstream consumption.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if the fixture would access real files or devices, requires out-of-bounds memory access, or cannot be represented as bounded synthetic views.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding child view construction to validated parent length generation, the phase-drift fixture is rejected while the consistent positive control remains accepted.
scenarios.parser_input_phase_generation: Record parent input generation, parent parser instance, child parser instance, framing/body phase generations, and child semantic-object generation.
scenarios.transition_invariant_trace: Capture the transition where parent metadata authorizes a child view, expected length invariant, later child interpretation, and first generation mismatch.
scenarios.structural_metadata_semantic_object: Bind parent length, child length, region/view identity, normalized values, and the exact child semantic object generated from the controlled slice.
scenarios.recovery_deferred_validation_state: Record whether length agreement is validated immediately or deferred; no recovery path should obscure the parent-to-child generation relationship.
scenarios.nested_cross_record_provenance: Bind parent artifact identity to the child slice/view, child parser instance, ownership, remapping generation, and returned semantic object lineage.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the read-only child semantic consumer that observes the controlled inconsistent view and emits only structured synthetic metadata.
scenarios.effective_semantic_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to read-only semantic consumption of a child object built under mismatched parent and child length generations.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result contains only synthetic child object identity, parent/child generation tags, and normalized length metadata with no unsafe memory access.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate parent generation, child parser generation, validated region identity, semantic object, downstream consumer, and read-only receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold parent/child bytes constant and change only the parent length generation or validation binding, then compare acceptance and semantic-object identity.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject out-of-bounds access, integer overflow, independent child-buffer ownership, harness slicing mistakes, or a different nested parser instance as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: PS3 because an inert downstream consumer accepts a child semantic object produced under mismatched parent and child phase generations.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PS3 maximum unless a stronger bounded semantic effect and complete nested provenance, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation evidence are demonstrated.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic forward reference is created under parser generation N and later resolved under generation N+1 without revalidating the originating state assumptions.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock read-only linker resolves only synthetic record IDs and returns a structured object-identity receipt without executing or mutating external resources.
scenarios.positive_control: A reference created and resolved within the same current parser generation links to the intended synthetic target and produces a matching semantic object.
scenarios.negative_control: A reference whose target ID is absent is rejected by the mock linker before any linked semantic object reaches the downstream consumer.
scenarios.stop_condition: Do not proceed if reference resolution touches external resources, becomes nondeterministic, or requires unsafe execution instead of synthetic object linking.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding deferred resolution to the originating parser-state generation, stale references are rejected while same-generation valid references still resolve.
scenarios.parser_input_phase_generation: Record input artifact generation, parser instance, source-record phase/state generation, deferred resolution pass, and target-record generation.
scenarios.transition_invariant_trace: Trace reference creation, deferred queueing, state-generation advance, resolution transition, expected origin invariant, and first stale-generation acceptance.
scenarios.structural_metadata_semantic_object: Bind source record ID, target record ID, resolution table generation, and final linked semantic object identity and generation.
scenarios.recovery_deferred_validation_state: Record deferred-validation and resolution generations explicitly, including whether any recovery path or warning modified the source reference state.
scenarios.nested_cross_record_provenance: Capture source record, target record, cross-record mapping, resolution generation, duplicate/cycle policy, and final linked object provenance.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the mock read-only consumer that receives the linked semantic object and reports source/target generations in a deterministic receipt.
scenarios.effective_semantic_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to semantic linkage using a stale originating parser generation in a fully synthetic cross-record fixture.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one read-only linked-object receipt naming source, target, and resolution generations without external or executable behavior.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind source parser state, deferred resolution generation, target record identity, linked semantic object, consumer identity, and receipt in one causal tuple.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold source and target records constant while changing only origin-generation revalidation at resolution time, then compare stale versus current acceptance.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject missing target semantics, documented generation-independent references, duplicate policy, stale logs, or a safely rebuilt source object as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: PS3 because the read-only linker and downstream consumer accept a semantic reference created under a stale parser-state generation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PS3 maximum until a bounded semantic effect and complete cross-record provenance, counterfactuals, receipt binding, and remediation replay support promotion.
